name: Science Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public scientific research data.

entries.title: CERN Open Data Portal
entries.description: Petabyte-scale open access to particle-physics datasets, software, and documentation from CERN's LHC experiments (ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, LHCb, and others), released for research and education.

access.auth_note: Some derived research/analysis tools require a free CERN Open Data account; raw dataset browsing and download do not.

coverage.spatial: global (international collaboration; hosted at CERN, Switzerland/France)

entries.notes: Verified reachable this session (HTTP 200). Seeded as this vertical's first international (non-US) source per operator request to seed the new verticals international-first.

entries.title: NASA Exoplanet Archive
entries.description: NASA's catalog of confirmed exoplanets and their host stars, plus mission data from Kepler, K2, TESS, and ground-based surveys, served through interactive tables, a TAP interface, an API, and bulk downloads.
entries.publisher: NASA Exoplanet Science Institute (NExScI), Caltech/IPAC, for NASA
entries.license: unverified — no license stated; the archive asks for a standard acknowledgment in publications
entries.attribution: This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with NASA under the Exoplanet Exploration Program.
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page reports "6,451 Confirmed Planets" as of 10/15/2026 and lists a Table Access Protocol (TAP) interface, an API, and bulk data download. The acknowledgment page (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/acknowledge.html) gives the standard acknowledgment text, used here as the attribution. It's operated by Caltech under NASA contract, so the jurisdiction is recorded as national (US). Several details come from the archive's usual practice, not from these pages: the weekly cadence and the votable/json formats. No license is stated, so none is claimed.

entries.title: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)
entries.description: NASA's long-term archive of digital data from planetary science missions — Mars, Juno, Dawn, InSight, Artemis, and more — curated by discipline nodes and released to the public on a regular schedule.
entries.publisher: U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Planetary Data System

coverage.temporal: decades of planetary missions to present

entries.license: unverified — NASA mission data; no license stated on the PDS home page
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page lists recent data releases, among them "Artemis II Mission Data" (October 7, 2026) and earlier Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Juno, Dawn, InSight, and Odyssey releases. The archive is built on the PDS4 (and legacy PDS3) standards. API availability comes from PDS's usual search services and wasn't checked. NASA data is generally released without restriction, but no license is stated here, so the license is left unverified.

entries.title: NSF National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES)
entries.description: The U.S. federal statistical agency for science and engineering: surveys and data on research and development funding and performance, the science and engineering workforce, STEM education, and innovation, including the Science and Engineering Indicators.
entries.publisher: U.S. National Science Foundation, National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics (NCSES)

coverage.spatial: United States (with international comparisons in Indicators)

entries.attribution: National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics, National Science Foundation
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page lists areas of interest (Innovation & Global Competitiveness, Research & Development Funding & Performance, Science & Engineering Workforce, STEM Education), a surveys catalog, a release schedule, and a data explorer. NCSES runs many surveys, each on its own schedule, so cadence is event. The formats are assumed from NCSES's usual table downloads and weren't checked.

entries.title: USGS Earthquake Catalog (ComCat) Event Web Service
entries.description: The USGS Advanced National Seismic System comprehensive earthquake catalog, queryable through an FDSN Event Web Service by time, location, magnitude, and more, with real-time GeoJSON feeds for recent events.
entries.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Earthquake Hazards Program

coverage.spatial: global (most complete for the United States)

entries.attribution: U.S. Geological Survey, ANSS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat)
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page describes "an implementation of the FDSN Event Web Service Specification" for custom earthquake searches and recommends the Real-time GeoJSON Feeds for automated display. Two things come from the service's usual documentation, not this page: the output formats and the name ComCat. The catalog updates continuously; the schema has no continuous value, so cadence is recorded as daily.
